sections.markdown:
## C2 — Traffic sign shapes, colors and signals
FACT_ID: sec16-R01 | anchor: A01
An Emergency Notification Sign, or ENS, is for crossing emergencies that may require train traffic to stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-R02 | anchor: A01
Track obstructions and malfunctioning crossing lights or gates are examples of emergencies addressed by an ENS. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-R03 | anchor: A01
Guide signs tell drivers their location, road and route toward a destination. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-R04 | anchor: A01
Most guide signs are rectangular, but county-road signs and freeway route markers may have different shapes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-R05 | anchor: A01
A guide sign's information type determines its color in the source description. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec16-R06 | anchor: A02
At a red light, stop behind the crosswalk or stop line. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec16-R07 | anchor: A02
A right turn on red is allowed only after stopping and yielding to people and other vehicles, unless a sign prohibits it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec16-R08 | anchor: A02
A left turn on red from a one-way street to another one-way street is permitted after stopping and yielding. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec16-R09 | anchor: A02
At an amber light, stop before entering the intersection if that can be done safely; otherwise proceed carefully. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec16-R10 | anchor: A02
A green light permits entering only when the way is clear, while yielding to people and vehicles already in the intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec16-R11 | anchor: A02
A flashing red signal requires a complete stop before the intersection and has the same meaning as a stop sign. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec16-R12 | anchor: A02
A flashing amber signal requires caution at the warned hazardous intersection or location. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec16-R13 | anchor: A02
A red arrow prohibits turning in the direction it points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec16-R14 | anchor: A02
An amber arrow may follow a green arrow and warns drivers to clear the intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec16-R15 | anchor: A02
A green arrow permits turning in its direction without stopping when the path is clear, but drivers must yield to people and other traffic already inside the intersection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0097]
